title: Primitive Obsession with Multi-Argument Homogeneous Types
pattern: A function signature contains consecutive parameters of the same primitive type, requiring callers to manually match the positional order.
why_bad: The compiler cannot verify if the arguments are swapped. Senders must memorize the positional convention, leading to silent and hard-to-detect logic bugs.
detection: A function signature has consecutive parameters of identical types (e.g., multiple strings or doubles) with distinct semantic meanings.
counterexample: Using single-variant enums or strong newtype wrappers to differentiate parameters.
fix: Wrap parameters in distinct newtypes: `fn add(user: User, group: Group)` where `User` and `Group` are separate tuple structs.
source: Martin, Clean Code, p. 189 [189]; or Heather Adkins, p. 265 [374-375].
